questions.question: What is the function of a capacitor bank?
questions.tutor: Capacitor bank supplies reactive power to improve power factor.

questions.question: What is a reactor in power systems?
questions.tutor: Reactor (inductor) limits fault current or filters harmonics.

questions.question: What is a busbar?
questions.tutor: Busbar is a metallic strip for distributing electrical power to feeders.

questions.question: What is a switchgear?
choices: Combination of switching and protection devices
questions.tutor: Switchgear includes breakers, switches, fuses, and relays for control and protection.

questions.question: What is the difference between switchgear and switchboard?
choices: Switchgear has drawout breakers; switchboard has fixed
questions.tutor: Switchgear typically has drawout circuit breakers; switchboards have fixed mounted.

questions.question: What is a VFD?
questions.tutor: VFD controls motor speed by varying frequency and voltage.

questions.question: What is a soft starter?
questions.tutor: Soft starter gradually increases voltage to reduce inrush current.

questions.question: What is a UPS?
questions.tutor: UPS provides backup power during utility failure.

questions.question: What is the difference between online and offline UPS?
choices: Online always powers load from inverter; offline switches on failure
questions.tutor: Online UPS (double conversion) supplies conditioned power continuously; offline switches only when needed.

questions.question: What is a battery charger?
choices: Converts AC to DC for charging batteries
questions.tutor: Battery charger supplies controlled DC current to recharge batteries.

questions.question: What is a servo motor?
questions.tutor: Servo motor uses feedback (encoder) for precise position/speed control.

questions.question: What is a stepper motor?
questions.tutor: Stepper motor rotates in fixed angular steps, used in printers and CNC.

questions.question: What is a contactor?
choices: Electrically controlled switch for heavy loads
questions.tutor: Contactor is a relay for switching high-power circuits (motors, heaters).

questions.question: What is a relay?
choices: Electrically operated switch for low power
questions.tutor: Relay uses small control signal to switch a larger circuit.

questions.question: What is a PLC?
questions.tutor: PLC is industrial computer for automation and control.

questions.question: What is a transducer?
choices: Converts one form of energy to another
questions.tutor: Transducer converts physical quantity (pressure, temp) to electrical signal.

questions.question: What is a thermistor?
questions.tutor: Thermistor resistance changes with temperature (NTC or PTC).

questions.question: What is a varistor?
questions.tutor: Varistor (MOV) clamps voltage spikes, used for surge protection.

questions.question: What is an LVDT?
questions.tutor: LVDT measures linear displacement using mutual inductance.

questions.question: What is an encoder?
questions.tutor: Encoder provides feedback on motor shaft position and speed.

questions.question: What is a resistor?
questions.tutor: Resistor limits current and dissipates power as heat.

questions.question: What is a potentiometer?
questions.tutor: Potentiometer (pot) is an adjustable voltage divider or variable resistor.

questions.question: What is a solenoid?
questions.tutor: Solenoid converts electrical energy into linear mechanical motion.

questions.question: What is a hall effect sensor?
questions.tutor: Hall sensor detects magnetic field and outputs proportional voltage.

questions.question: What is an SCR?
questions.tutor: SCR is a latching semiconductor switch used in power control (rectifiers, dimmers).
